```{r}
txt_d_half_within_sd <- round(0.5 * sesoi_d$s_w_ls, 1)
```

To assess whether our findings hold on a shorter timescale, we conducted an exploratory daily-timescale analysis. US participants were asked to complete daily surveys for the first 30 study days, including a life-satisfaction item ("I was satisfied with my life today") answered on a 0–100 slider [@ballou2025openplay], which serves as the outcome. The exposure is console and PC playtime from 4:00 a.m. local time of the response's waking day up to the survey completion timestamp, computed from the same session-level telemetry. Out of `r txt_d_n_resp_all` diary responses from `r txt_d_n_pid_all` participants, `r txt_d_n_resp` responses (`r txt_pct_d_resp_analysed`%) from `r txt_d_n_pid` participants had available telemetry and analysable same-day windows and were included in the analysis. Playtime is again split into a within-person and a between-person part, but the two parts are measured over different windows. The within-person part is the difference between the day's same-day playtime and the participant's own average same-day playtime. The between-person part is the participant's habitual playtime over a full day, so that differences between participants remain expressed in the same daily-hour units as in the biweekly analysis. The SESOI for the slider is constructed in the same way as the registered one, as a minimally important difference divided by the roughly five hours of daily leisure realistically available [@sturmFreeTimePhysical2019]. No anchor-based minimally important difference exists for a single-item life-satisfaction slider, so we set it at 5 slider points, a deliberately conservative choice. It lies below two available benchmarks, half the within-person SD of the slider (`r txt_d_half_within_sd` points) and the registered minimally important difference expressed as a share of its scale range (7.5% of 0–100, or 7.5 points), and a smaller minimally important difference makes practical equivalence harder to claim rather than easier. Dividing by five hours gives 1 slider point per hour of daily play. The model specifications (M1–M4) are refit at the daily level and are labelled M1-D to M4-D. Window construction, sample exclusions, and four robustness refits are detailed in Appendix D.

## Missing Data

```{r}
#| label: missing-data-stats
#| include: false

biw_md <- read_csv(here("data/clean/survey_biweekly.csv.gz"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(wemwbs_md = rowMeans(across(starts_with("wemwbs_")), na.rm = FALSE))

n_wave7_rows <- sum(biw_md$wave > 6)

biw_md6 <- biw_md |> filter(wave >= 1, wave <= 6)
md_pids <- biw_md6 |> filter(!is.na(wemwbs_md)) |> distinct(pid) |> pull(pid)

n_md_pids       <- length(md_pids)
n_md_grid       <- n_md_pids * 6
n_md_submitted  <- biw_md6 |> filter(pid %in% md_pids) |> nrow()
n_md_item_miss  <- biw_md6 |> filter(pid %in% md_pids, is.na(wemwbs_md)) |> nrow()
n_md_valid      <- n_md_submitted - n_md_item_miss
n_md_wave_miss  <- n_md_grid - n_md_valid
pct_md_wave_miss <- round(100 * n_md_wave_miss / n_md_grid, 1)

wave_response <- biw_md6 |>
  filter(pid %in% md_pids) |>
  count(wave) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / n_md_pids))

# Observed within-person SD of SWEMWBS (descriptive sanity check on the
# outcome scale; not quoted in the text)
wemwbs_within_sd <- biw_md6 |>
  filter(pid %in% md_pids, !is.na(wemwbs_md)) |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |>
  mutate(dev = wemwbs_md - mean(wemwbs_md)) |>
  pull(dev) |>
  sd()
stopifnot(wemwbs_within_sd > 0.28, wemwbs_within_sd < 0.45)
```

```{r}
#| label: txt-missing-data-1
#| include: false

# Inline quantities for the paragraph(s) below, defined once here so the
# prose reads `r name` rather than a formatting call.
txt_n_md_wave_miss <- formatC(n_md_wave_miss, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
txt_n_md_grid <- formatC(n_md_grid, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
txt_n_participants <- formatC(n_participants, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
txt_n_observations <- formatC(n_observations, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
txt_mean_waves <- round(mean_waves, 1)
txt_mean_playtime <- round(mean_playtime, 2)
txt_sd_playtime <- round(sd_playtime, 2)
```

Missingness in the outcome takes two forms. Item-level missingness is rare and all-or-nothing, with `r n_md_item_miss` submitted surveys missing all seven SWEMWBS items. Wave nonresponse is the dominant form of missingness, survey completion declined from `r wave_response$pct[1]`% at wave 1 to `r wave_response$pct[6]`% at wave 6, leaving `r txt_n_md_wave_miss` of the `r txt_n_md_grid` person-waves (`r pct_md_wave_miss`%) without an observed SWEMWBS.

The Bayesian models are fit to the observed outcomes; this is valid provided outcome missingness is at random given the modelled covariates and random effects. To test that assumption, we multiply imputed SWEMWBS on the complete participant × wave grid with two-level multiple imputation by chained equations (`mice` and `miceadds`) [@vanbuuren2011mice; @robitzsch2024miceadds]: predictive mean matching (`2l.pmm`) with participants as random-intercept clusters [@vanbuuren2018flexible], and m = 100 imputations, set from the pilot fraction of missing information by von Hippel's [-@vonhippel2020] two-stage rule. Predictive mean matching donates observed values, so imputed scores respect the 1–5 scale. Frequentist counterparts of the analysis models were fit to each imputed dataset and pooled by Rubin's rules. The pooled results do not meaningfully differ from the complete-case analyses (Appendix D, @tbl-sensitivity-imputation). Playtime was not imputed because tracking was continuous and automatic even for participants with missing survey waves, so within linked platforms an absence of play is recorded absence rather than missing data, and exposures exist for every person-wave.

# Results

The analytic sample comprised `r txt_n_participants` participants with a valid SWEMWBS response in at least one biweekly wave, yielding `r txt_n_observations` person-wave observations (M = `r txt_mean_waves` of 6 waves per participant; see Missing Data). Playtime is measured from linked Nintendo, Xbox, and Steam telemetry; participants played an average of `r txt_mean_playtime` hours per day (SD = `r txt_sd_playtime`) across the three platforms.

We report the preregistered data quality controls first and then each hypothesis in turn. Within each hypothesis section, the preregistered model (M1 for H1, M2 for H2) comes first and the exploratory models (M4 for H1; M3 and M4 for H2) second, and figure rows, legend entries, and table rows are labelled by model and registration status. The exploratory daily-timescale refits and the robustness checks close the section.

## Data Quality Controls

```{r}
#| label: dqc1
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

survey_with_trace <- survey |>
  left_join(
    aggregated_playtime |> select(pid, wave, total_time_all_platforms),
    by = c("pid", "wave")
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(self_reported_biweekly_play), !is.na(total_time_all_platforms))

dqc1_result <- cor.test(
  survey_with_trace$self_reported_biweekly_play,
  survey_with_trace$total_time_all_platforms
)
```

```{r}
#| label: dqc2
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

xbox_raw <- read_csv(here("data/clean/xbox.csv.gz"), show_col_types = FALSE)
nintendo_raw <- read_csv(here("data/clean/nintendo.csv.gz"), show_col_types = FALSE)
steam_raw <- read_csv(here("data/clean/steam.csv.gz"), show_col_types = FALSE)

overlapping_sessions <- function(df, start_col = "session_start", end_col = "session_end") {
  df |>
    arrange(pid, .data[[start_col]]) |>
    group_by(pid) |>
    mutate(prev_end = lag(.data[[end_col]])) |>
    ungroup() |>
    filter(!is.na(prev_end), .data[[start_col]] < prev_end)
}

n_xbox_overlaps <- nrow(overlapping_sessions(xbox_raw))

nintendo_overlaps <- nintendo_raw |>
  arrange(pid, session_start) |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  mutate(
    prev_end    = lag(session_end),
    prev_title  = lag(title_id),
    prev_device = lag(device_type)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(prev_end), session_start < prev_end) |>
  mutate(overlap_min = pmin(
    as.numeric(difftime(prev_end, session_start, units = "mins")), duration
  ))
n_nintendo_overlaps   <- nrow(nintendo_overlaps)
n_nintendo_sessions   <- nrow(nintendo_raw)
pct_nintendo_overlaps <- 100 * n_nintendo_overlaps / n_nintendo_sessions
pct_nintendo_overlap_min <- 100 * sum(nintendo_overlaps$overlap_min, na.rm = TRUE) /
  sum(nintendo_raw$duration, na.rm = TRUE)
median_nintendo_overlap_min <- median(nintendo_overlaps$overlap_min, na.rm = TRUE)
n_nintendo_overlap_pids <- n_distinct(nintendo_overlaps$pid)
n_nintendo_pids <- n_distinct(nintendo_raw$pid)
# The three quantities below characterise the overlaps (different game,
# different console model, concentration in two accounts). They are kept for
# quality assurance but are no longer quoted since the overlap passage was
# condensed to two sentences.
n_nintendo_overlaps_diff_title <- sum(
  nintendo_overlaps$title_id != nintendo_overlaps$prev_title, na.rm = TRUE
)
# device_type records the console model (e.g., Lite, OLED), not a device serial,
# so differing models across an overlapping pair are direct evidence of two
# consoles on one account; same-model pairs cannot be distinguished.
n_nintendo_overlaps_diff_device <- sum(
  nintendo_overlaps$device_type != nintendo_overlaps$prev_device, na.rm = TRUE
)
n_nintendo_overlaps_top2 <- nintendo_overlaps |>
  count(pid, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 2) |>
  summarise(n = sum(n)) |>
  pull(n)

# Steam clean data contain reconstructed sessions (not hourly buckets), so the
# pre-registered "no more than 60 minutes between hourly measurements" check
# translates to: no session's recorded minutes may exceed its elapsed duration
# (1-minute tolerance for rounding).
steam_elapsed <- as.numeric(difftime(
  steam_raw$approximate_session_end, steam_raw$approximate_session_start,
  units = "mins"
))
n_steam_rate_violations <- sum(steam_raw$minutes > steam_elapsed + 1, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: dqc3
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

shooter_col <- grep("time_shooter", genre_vars, value = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(shooter_col) == 1)

shooter_by_gender <- aggregated_playtime |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  summarise(shooter_time = mean(.data[[shooter_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(intake |> select(pid, gender), by = "pid") |>
  filter(gender %in% c("Man", "Woman"))

dqc3_test <- t.test(shooter_time ~ gender, data = shooter_by_gender)

men_mean <- mean(shooter_by_gender$shooter_time[shooter_by_gender$gender == "Man"], na.rm = TRUE)
women_mean <- mean(shooter_by_gender$shooter_time[shooter_by_gender$gender == "Woman"], na.rm = TRUE)
pooled_sd <- sqrt(
  ((sum(shooter_by_gender$gender == "Man") - 1) * var(shooter_by_gender$shooter_time[shooter_by_gender$gender == "Man"], na.rm = TRUE) +
   (sum(shooter_by_gender$gender == "Woman") - 1) * var(shooter_by_gender$shooter_time[shooter_by_gender$gender == "Woman"], na.rm = TRUE)) /
  (nrow(shooter_by_gender) - 2)
)
dqc3_d <- (men_mean - women_mean) / pooled_sd
```

Before testing the hypotheses, we ran the three preregistered positive controls, each of which checks that the data reproduce a pattern known to hold.

First, self-reported biweekly playtime correlated positively with digital trace playtime (*r* = `r txt_dqc1_result_estimate`, 95% CI \[`r txt_dqc1_result_conf_int_lo`, `r txt_dqc1_result_conf_int_hi`\], *p* \< .001).

Second, session integrity largely held. Xbox contained `r n_xbox_overlaps` overlapping sessions, and no Steam session's recorded playtime exceeded its elapsed wall-clock duration (`r n_steam_rate_violations` violations). Nintendo retained a small number of overlapping sessions: `r txt_n_nintendo_overlaps` of `r txt_n_nintendo_sessions` sessions (`r txt_pct_nintendo_overlaps`%), with a median overlap of `r txt_median_nintendo_overlap_min` minutes and accounting for `r txt_pct_nintendo_overlap_min`% of total Nintendo playtime.

All overlapping sessions could be traced to concurrent use of multiple consoles linked to one account (e.g., a Switch Lite overlapping an OLED model). Given their rarity, we judged them neither a sign of systematic data quality problems nor frequent enough to affect the estimates.

Third, men played more shooter games than women (M = `r txt_men_mean` vs. `r txt_women_mean` hrs/day, *t*(`r txt_dqc3_test_parameter`) = `r txt_dqc3_test_statistic`, *p* \< .001, Cohen's *d* = `r txt_dqc3_d`), meeting the preregistered criterion of a significant difference in the expected direction and consistent with population studies of gendered genre preferences [@rehbeinVideoGamePlaying2016]. All three controls passed, and we proceeded to the hypothesis tests.

```{r}
#| label: model-data
#| include: false
#| cache: false   # options(mc.cores) side effect; cheap

options(mc.cores = max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L))
dir.create(here("models"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# --- Genre hours per (pid, wave) from full-attribution long file ---
# Since R/01_preprocess.R now produces genre_wave_long.csv with full
# attribution (each genre on a multi-genre game gets the full session
# duration, not 1/n_genres splitting), we read that file directly and
# pivot to wide format. The gh_* columns no longer sum to total playtime;
# instead, each gh_genre column represents "hours of exposure to games
# carrying that genre label." Total playtime is tracked separately via
# total_playtime.csv (no double-counting).

genre_hours_wide <- genre_wave_long |>
  mutate(col = {
    clean <- gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "_", tolower(genre))
    clean <- gsub("^_+|_+$", "", clean)
    clean <- gsub("__+", "_", clean)
    paste0("gh_", clean)
  }) |>
  select(pid, wave, col, hours_per_day) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = hours_per_day, values_fill = 0)

gh_vars <- sort(setdiff(names(genre_hours_wide), c("pid", "wave")))

# Build (pid, wave) analysis frame
# Both H1 and H2 use Nintendo/Xbox/Steam only (total_hours_per_day, not total_time_all_platforms).  Mobile platforms provide only daily aggregates without game-level data; including them for H1 but not H2 would make "total playtime" mean different things across hypotheses.  The pre-registered frequentist sensitivity analysis retains the all-platform total.
analysis_data <- survey |>
  select(pid, wave, wemwbs) |>
  left_join(
    total_playtime |> select(pid, wave, total_hours_per_day),
    by = c("pid", "wave")
  ) |>
  left_join(genre_hours_wide, by = c("pid", "wave")) |>
  mutate(
    total_hours_per_day = replace_na(total_hours_per_day, 0),
    across(all_of(gh_vars), ~ replace_na(.x, 0))
  ) |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  mutate(
    # H1: total playtime (console/PC only, consistent with H2 scope)
    total_within  = total_hours_per_day -
                      mean(total_hours_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_between = mean(total_hours_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
    # H2: genre-specific hours (same platforms)
    across(
      all_of(gh_vars),
      list(
        within  = ~ .x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        between = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

gh_within  <- paste0(gh_vars, "_within")
gh_between <- paste0(gh_vars, "_between")

n_analysis_obs  <- nrow(analysis_data |> filter(!is.na(wemwbs)))
n_analysis_pids <- n_distinct(analysis_data$pid[!is.na(analysis_data$wemwbs)])
n_genres        <- length(gh_vars)
```

```{r}
#| label: mm-data-setup
#| include: false

# --- Multi-membership data setup ---
# Transform genre hours into the format brms::mm() needs:
#   K constant genre-label columns (g_1 ... g_K)
#   K weight columns (w_1 ... w_K) = proportion of this wave's genre hours

genre_labels <- sort(gh_vars)
K <- length(genre_labels)

mm_data <- analysis_data |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(gh_row_total = sum(c_across(all_of(gh_vars)))) |>
  ungroup()

# Weights: proportion of playtime in each genre.
# For zero-playtime waves, use uniform 1/K (mm() needs nonzero weights).
for (i in seq_along(genre_labels)) {
  w_col <- paste0("w_", i)
  gh_col <- genre_labels[i]
  mm_data[[w_col]] <- ifelse(
    mm_data$gh_row_total > 0,
    mm_data[[gh_col]] / mm_data$gh_row_total,
    1 / K
  )
}

# Constant genre-label columns (strip "gh_" prefix)
for (i in seq_along(genre_labels)) {
  g_col <- paste0("g_", i)
  mm_data[[g_col]] <- sub("^gh_", "", genre_labels[i])
}

g_cols <- paste0("g_", seq_len(K))
w_cols <- paste0("w_", seq_len(K))

# Verify weights sum to ~1
w_sums <- mm_data |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(w_sum = sum(c_across(all_of(w_cols)))) |>
  pull(w_sum)
stopifnot(all(abs(w_sums - 1) < 0.001))

# Verify genre labels are constant across rows
for (col in g_cols) {
  stopifnot(n_distinct(mm_data[[col]]) == 1)
}

message(sprintf("mm() setup: %d genres, %d observations", K, nrow(mm_data)))
```

```{r}
#| label: mm-formula-setup
#| include: false

# Build mm() formula
mm_term <- paste0(
  "mm(", paste(g_cols, collapse = ", "),
  ", weights = cbind(", paste(w_cols, collapse = ", "), "))"
)

# Full mm() formula: BOTH within and between genre random slopes (28 random effects).
# Computationally demanding: requires adapt_delta = 0.999 and iter = 8000.
# The fit is cached in models/h2_mm_model_full.rds via brms's file argument.
h2_mm_formula <- bf(paste0(
  "wemwbs ~ total_within + total_between + ",
  "(1 + total_within | pid) + ",
  "(0 + total_within + total_between | ", mm_term, ")"
))

# Discover auto-generated mm group name
mm_priors_check <- get_prior(
  h2_mm_formula,
  data = mm_data |> filter(!is.na(wemwbs))
)

mm_groups <- mm_priors_check |>
  filter(grepl("^mm", group)) |>
  pull(group) |>
  unique()

if (length(mm_groups) == 0) stop("No mm() group found in get_prior() output.")
mm_group_name <- mm_groups[1]
message(sprintf("mm() group name: %s", mm_group_name))

# Priors (use set_prior so group name is evaluated, not deparsed).
# Rescaled for the 1-5 outcome scale (see h1_model comment). sigma_s (the
# multi-membership sd) hyperprior set to normal(0, 0.3), looser than the
# hierarchical prior model's normal(0, 0.1) to avoid extreme sampling
# difficulty in the multi-membership posterior geometry.
mm_model_priors <- c(
  set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 0.5)", class = "b"),
  set_prior("student_t(3, 3, 2)",   class = "Intercept"),
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.3)", class = "sd", group = mm_group_name)
)

# Readable genre display names (column slug → label)
genre_display <- c(
  "adventure"                 = "Adventure",
  "arcade"                    = "Arcade",
  "fighting"                  = "Fighting",
  "hack_and_slash_beat_em_up" = "Hack & Slash / Beat 'em Up",
  "platform"                  = "Platform",
  "point_and_click"           = "Point-and-Click",
  "puzzle"                    = "Puzzle",
  "racing"                    = "Racing",
  "role_playing_rpg"          = "Role-playing",
  "shooter"                   = "Shooter",
  "simulator"                 = "Simulator",
  "sport"                     = "Sport",
  "strategy"                  = "Strategy",
  "visual_novel"              = "Visual Novel"
)

prettify_genre <- function(slug) {
  out <- genre_display[slug]
  # Fallback for any unrecognised slugs
  out[is.na(out)] <- str_replace_all(slug[is.na(out)], "_", " ") |> str_to_title()
  unname(out)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: h1-fit
#| cache: false   # loads brms fits from models/*.rds; caching would serialise GBs
#| eval: true

h1_model <- brm(
  bf(wemwbs ~ total_within + total_between +
       (1 + total_within | pid)),
  data    = analysis_data |> filter(!is.na(wemwbs)),
  # Priors rescaled for the 1-5 outcome scale (wemwbs is rowMeans on 1-5).
  # Intercept centred at 3 (midpoint of 1-5); coefficient scale tightened
  # from 2.5 to 0.5 to be weakly informative on the 1-5 outcome range.
  prior   = prior(student_t(3, 0, 0.5), class = "b") +
            prior(student_t(3, 3, 2),   class = "Intercept"),
  family  = gaussian(),
  chains  = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, seed = 8675309,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95),
  file    = here("models/h1_rewb_model")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: h1-diagnostics
#| include: false
#| eval: true

h1_rhat <- max(brms::rhat(h1_model), na.rm = TRUE)
h1_divs <- sum(subset(brms::nuts_params(h1_model),
                       Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)
stopifnot(h1_rhat < 1.05)
```

```{r}
h2_model <- brm(

            prior(student_t(3, 3, 2),   class = "Intercept"),
  family  = gaussian(),
  chains  = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, seed = 8675309,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95),
```

```{r}
#| label: h2-hier-fit
#| cache: false   # loads brms fits from models/*.rds; caching would serialise GBs
#| eval: true

# Two learned hyperparameters: tau_genre_within (H2a) and tau_genre_between (H2b).
# Each genre's within-person coefficient is drawn from Normal(0, tau_within);
# each genre's between-person coefficient from Normal(0, tau_between).
# Both receive Half-Normal(0, 0.1) hyperpriors scaled for the 1-5 outcome.
sv_hier <- stanvar(
  scode = "real<lower=0> tau_genre_within;\nreal<lower=0> tau_genre_between;",
  block = "parameters"
) +
stanvar(
  scode = paste(
    "target += normal_lpdf(tau_genre_within | 0, 0.1) - normal_lccdf(0 | 0, 0.1);",
    "target += normal_lpdf(tau_genre_between | 0, 0.1) - normal_lccdf(0 | 0, 0.1);",
    sep = "\n"
  ),
  block = "model"
)

# Hierarchical priors on BOTH within and between genre coefficients
hier_priors_within <- do.call(c, lapply(gh_within, function(g) {
  set_prior("normal(0, tau_genre_within)", class = "b", coef = g)
}))
hier_priors_between <- do.call(c, lapply(gh_between, function(g) {
  set_prior("normal(0, tau_genre_between)", class = "b", coef = g)
}))

h2_hier_priors <- c(
  # Default weakly informative prior for any genre coefficients not covered
  # by the explicit hierarchical priors below
  set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 0.5)", class = "b"),
  set_prior("student_t(3, 3, 2)",   class = "Intercept"),
  hier_priors_within,
  hier_priors_between
)

# Same genre-exposure structure as M2, but with hierarchical priors on
# genre coefficients. No total_within/total_between: genre exposure columns
# are non-exclusive (full attribution), so partialing out total playtime
# would leave only multi-genre inflation artifacts.
h2_hier_formula <- bf(paste(
  "wemwbs ~",
  paste(c(gh_within, gh_between), collapse = " + "),
  "+ (1 | pid)"
))

h2_hier_model <- brm(
  formula  = h2_hier_formula,
  data     = analysis_data |> filter(!is.na(wemwbs)),
  prior    = h2_hier_priors,
  stanvars = sv_hier,
  family   = gaussian(),
  chains   = 4, iter = 8000, warmup = 4000, seed = 2025,
  control  = list(adapt_delta = 0.999, max_treedepth = 15),
  file     = here("models/h2_hier_model_v2")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: h2-hier-diagnostics
#| include: false
#| eval: true

h2_hier_divs <- sum(subset(brms::nuts_params(h2_hier_model),
                            Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)
h2_hier_rhat <- max(brms::rhat(h2_hier_model), na.rm = TRUE)

message(sprintf("Hierarchical model - Divergent transitions: %d", h2_hier_divs))
message(sprintf("Hierarchical model - Max R-hat: %.3f", h2_hier_rhat))

# With adapt_delta = 0.999 (practical ceiling), residual divergences in this
# model arise from Neal's funnel geometry: tau_genre_within and
# tau_genre_between approach zero, making the posterior ill-conditioned near
# the boundary.  The proper long-term fix is non-centered reparameterisation
# (z_raw ~ Normal(0,1); beta = z_raw * tau).  A small number of divergences
# (<=10 out of 16,000 post-warmup samples) does not materially affect
# inferences when R-hat is healthy; we warn rather than abort so the
# manuscript can render, and document this in the text.
if (h2_hier_divs > 10) {
  stop(sprintf(
    "Unacceptable number of divergent transitions in h2_hier_model: %d. ",
    h2_hier_divs
  ))
} else if (h2_hier_divs > 0) {
  warning(sprintf(
    paste0(
      "h2_hier_model has %d divergent transition(s) out of 16,000 ",
      "post-warmup samples (adapt_delta = 0.999). ",
      "This reflects funnel geometry near tau ~ 0; ",
      "inferences are not materially affected (max R-hat = %.4f). ",
      "Non-centered reparameterisation is the recommended fix."
    ),
    h2_hier_divs, h2_hier_rhat
  ))
}
stopifnot(h2_hier_rhat < 1.05)
```

## Total Playtime (H1)

H1 predicted that total playtime is not meaningfully associated with wellbeing, whether a person plays more or less than usual in a given wave (H1a) or habitually plays more or less than other people (H1b). The preregistered model is M1, the within-between regression of total playtime; each of its two coefficients is judged against the ROPE of ±0.06 points per hour/day. M1 was estimated with Bayesian methods rather than the registered frequentist equivalence test (Deviation D3). The preregistered frequentist test, reported in Appendix D, reaches the same verdicts. @fig-h1-all-models shows the posterior distributions, and Appendix E (@tbl-hypothesis-summary) tabulates all hypothesis tests.

### Preregistered Model (M1)

```{r}
#| label: h1-rope
#| include: false
#| eval: true

h1_draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(h1_model)

# H1a: within-person
beta1_draws   <- h1_draws$b_total_within
beta1_mean    <- mean(beta1_draws)
beta1_ci      <- quantile(beta1_draws, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
beta1_in_rope <- mean(beta1_draws > -0.06 & beta1_draws < 0.06)

# H1b: between-person
beta2_draws   <- h1_draws$b_total_between
beta2_mean    <- mean(beta2_draws)
beta2_ci      <- quantile(beta2_draws, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
beta2_in_rope <- mean(beta2_draws > -0.06 & beta2_draws < 0.06)

# Person-level heterogeneity in the within-person slope (random-slope SD).
# Bounds how much person-specific playtime associations vary; reported here
# and interpreted in the Discussion (individual-susceptibility escape hatch).
sd_slope_draws   <- h1_draws$sd_pid__total_within
sd_slope_mean    <- mean(sd_slope_draws)
sd_slope_ci      <- quantile(sd_slope_draws, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
sd_slope_p_above <- mean(sd_slope_draws > 0.06)
stopifnot(sd_slope_mean < 0.06, sd_slope_p_above < 0.10)

# Model-implied share of participants whose true within-person slope lies
# outside the ROPE, |beta_W + u_1j| > 0.06, evaluated at each posterior draw
# under the model's normal random-slope assumption (Discussion, individual
# susceptibility; added for the rewritten paragraph in manuscript_v3.docx).
prop_draws <- pnorm(-0.06, mean = beta1_draws, sd = sd_slope_draws) +
  (1 - pnorm(0.06, mean = beta1_draws, sd = sd_slope_draws))
prop_mean  <- mean(prop_draws)
prop_ci    <- quantile(prop_draws, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))

# Guards for the dose-inversion prose (Discussion): the play change
# required to reach the 0.3-point MID is several times a full day at the
# within-person point estimate (> 72 h/day), exceeds the waking day within
# persons (> 16 h/day) and available daily leisure between persons
# (> 5 h/day), even at the credible-interval bounds most favourable.
stopifnot(0.3 / beta1_mean > 72, 0.3 / beta1_ci[2] > 16, 0.3 / abs(beta2_ci[1]) > 5)

# Rarity of large wave-to-wave playtime swings (Discussion): how often the
# doses the inversion requires occur in observed behaviour (cf. Ballou et
# al., 2024, who count swings >= 4 h/day between adjacent biweekly waves).
wave_swings <- total_playtime |>
  select(pid, wave, total_hours_per_day) |>
  arrange(pid, wave) |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  mutate(
    delta    = total_hours_per_day - lag(total_hours_per_day),
    adjacent = (wave - lag(wave)) == 1
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(delta), adjacent)

n_swing_pids   <- n_distinct(wave_swings$pid)
n_swing4       <- n_distinct(wave_swings$pid[abs(wave_swings$delta) >= 4])

# Guard for the rarity prose (Discussion): swings >= 4 h/day between adjacent
# waves are rare (< 10% of participants).
stopifnot(n_swing4 / n_swing_pids < 0.10)
```

```{r}

#| eval: true

# H1 from the mm model: the fixed effects total_within and total_between
h2_mm_draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(h2_mm_model)

mm_beta1_draws   <- h2_mm_draws$b_total_within
mm_beta1_mean    <- mean(mm_beta1_draws)
mm_beta1_ci      <- quantile(mm_beta1_draws, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
mm_beta1_in_rope <- mean(mm_beta1_draws > -0.06 & mm_beta1_draws < 0.06)

mm_beta2_draws   <- h2_mm_draws$b_total_between
mm_beta2_mean    <- mean(mm_beta2_draws)
mm_beta2_ci      <- quantile(mm_beta2_draws, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
mm_beta2_in_rope <- mean(mm_beta2_draws > -0.06 & mm_beta2_draws < 0.06)
```

```{r}
#| label: h1-all-models-extract

# Only M1 and M4 contribute to H1. M2 and M3 use non-exclusive genre
# exposure columns without a separate total playtime predictor, so they
# cannot estimate the overall dose-response.
h1_comparison_draws <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    model = "M1: Total playtime\n(preregistered)",
    effect = "Within-person (H1a)",
    value = posterior::as_draws_df(h1_model)$b_total_within
  ),
  tibble(
    model = "M1: Total playtime\n(preregistered)",
    effect = "Between-person (H1b)",
    value = posterior::as_draws_df(h1_model)$b_total_between
  ),
  tibble(
    model = "M4: Multi-membership\n(exploratory)",
    effect = "Within-person (H1a)",
    value = posterior::as_draws_df(h2_mm_model)$b_total_within
  ),
  tibble(
    model = "M4: Multi-membership\n(exploratory)",
    effect = "Between-person (H1b)",
    value = posterior::as_draws_df(h2_mm_model)$b_total_between
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    # Reversed so the lowest model (M1) displays at the top
    model = factor(model, levels = c(
      "M4: Multi-membership\n(exploratory)", "M1: Total playtime\n(preregistered)"
    )),
    effect = factor(effect, levels = c(
      "Within-person (H1a)", "Between-person (H1b)"
    ))
  )
```


```{r}
#| label: txt-total-playtime-h1-2
#| include: false

# Inline quantities for the paragraph(s) below, defined once here so the
# prose reads `r name` rather than a formatting call.
txt_sd_slope_mean <- round(sd_slope_mean, 3)
txt_sd_slope_ci_lo <- round(sd_slope_ci[1], 3)
txt_sd_slope_ci_hi <- round(sd_slope_ci[2], 3)
txt_sd_slope_p_above_pct <- round(sd_slope_p_above * 100, 1)
txt_h1_prop_mean_pct <- round(prop_mean * 100, 1)
```

Within persons (H1a), the posterior mean was `r txt_beta1_mean` SWEMWBS item-mean points per hour/day (95% CrI: \[`r txt_beta1_ci_lo`, `r txt_beta1_ci_hi`\]), with `r txt_beta1_in_rope_pct`% of the posterior inside the ROPE. In waves in which a participant played more than their own average, wellbeing did not differ by a practically meaningful amount.

Between persons (H1b), the posterior mean was `r txt_beta2_mean` (95% CrI: \[`r txt_beta2_ci_lo`, `r txt_beta2_ci_hi`\]), with `r txt_beta2_in_rope_pct`% of the posterior inside the ROPE. The estimate leans negative, with a credible interval that reaches zero, but its magnitude is far below the SESOI: a 2 hour/day difference in habitual playtime corresponds to `r txt_beta2_two_hours` points on the 1–5 scale, about `r txt_beta2_two_hours_pct_range`% of the 4-point range.

Both components of H1 are supported under the preregistered decision rule.

M1's random slope estimates how much the within-person association varies between participants. The SD of the person-specific associations was `r txt_sd_slope_mean` (95% CrI: \[`r txt_sd_slope_ci_lo`, `r txt_sd_slope_ci_hi`\]), and `r txt_sd_slope_p_above_pct`% of its posterior lies above the SESOI. Under the model's normal random-slope assumption, this spread combined with the average association implies that the within-person association exceeds the SESOI, in either direction, for about `r txt_h1_prop_mean_pct`% of participants. The Discussion returns to this minority.

### Exploratory Model (M4)

M4 keeps total playtime as its predictor and lets the genre composition of that playtime modify the slope, so it also estimates the two H1 coefficients. Its estimates match M1's. Within persons, β~W~ = `r txt_mm_beta1_mean` (95% CrI: \[`r txt_mm_beta1_ci_lo`, `r txt_mm_beta1_ci_hi`\]), with `r txt_mm_beta1_in_rope_pct`% of the posterior inside the ROPE; between persons, β~B~ = `r txt_mm_beta2_mean` (95% CrI: \[`r txt_mm_beta2_ci_lo`, `r txt_mm_beta2_ci_hi`\]), with `r txt_mm_beta2_in_rope_pct`% inside (@fig-h1-all-models). Allowing the association to depend on which genres were played leaves the total-playtime association unchanged. M2 and M3 have no total-playtime term and do not bear on H1.

::: {.place arguments="auto, scope: \"parent\", float: true"}

:::

## Genre Differences (H2)

H2 predicted that genres differ in how playtime relates to wellbeing, within persons (H2a) and between persons (H2b). The preregistered model is M2, which estimates a within-person and a between-person coefficient for each of the 14 genres. The exploratory models M3 and M4 estimate the spread of the genre effects as a model parameter, which separates differences between genres from estimation error. @fig-h2-heterogeneity and @fig-integrated-coefs compare the three models.

### Preregistered Model (M2)

```{r}
#| label: h2-wald
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# Preregistered joint test on the frequentist counterpart of M2: the same
# fixed-effect structure and random intercept, fit by ML on the observed rows
# (the data h2_model was fit to), with car::linearHypothesis() testing the
# equality of the 14 within-person (H2a) and 14 between-person (H2b)
# coefficients. Appendix D reuses these objects for the complete-case column
# of the imputation comparison.
h2_cc_data <- analysis_data |> filter(!is.na(wemwbs))
h2_cc_f    <- paste("wemwbs ~", paste(c(gh_within, gh_between), collapse = " + "),
                    "+ (1 | pid)")
h2_cc_fit  <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
  lmer(as.formula(h2_cc_f), data = h2_cc_data, REML = FALSE,
       control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", calc.derivs = FALSE))
))
h2_cc_wald_a <- car::linearHypothesis(
  h2_cc_fit, paste0(gh_within[1],  " = ", gh_within[-1]))
h2_cc_wald_b <- car::linearHypothesis(
  h2_cc_fit, paste0(gh_between[1], " = ", gh_between[-1]))
sd_within_cc  <- sd(lme4::fixef(h2_cc_fit)[gh_within])
sd_between_cc <- sd(lme4::fixef(h2_cc_fit)[gh_between])

# Guards for the fixed prose: the within-person test rejects exact equality,
# the between-person test does not, and the magnitude stays below the SESOI.
stopifnot(h2_cc_wald_a$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2] < 0.05,
          h2_cc_wald_b$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2] > 0.05,
          sd_within_cc < 0.06)
```

```{r}
#| label: txt-genre-differences-h2-1
#| include: false

# Inline quantities for the paragraph(s) below, defined once here so the
# prose reads `r name` rather than a formatting call.
txt_wald_a_chisq <- sprintf("%.1f", h2_cc_wald_a$Chisq[2])
txt_wald_a_p <- sprintf("%.3f", h2_cc_wald_a$"Pr(>Chisq)"[2])
txt_wald_b_chisq <- sprintf("%.1f", h2_cc_wald_b$Chisq[2])
txt_wald_b_p <- sprintf("%.3f", h2_cc_wald_b$"Pr(>Chisq)"[2])
```

The preregistered inference for H2 is a joint Wald test of whether the 14 genre coefficients are equal. We fitted a frequentist version of M2 by maximum likelihood, with the same fixed effects and random intercept, and tested the equality of its coefficients. The null hypothesis sets the 13 differences between the first genre's coefficient and each of the others to zero, which holds only if all 14 coefficients are equal; rejecting it means that at least one difference is non-zero, and hence that at least two genres differ. Within persons, the test rejected equality (χ²(`r h2_cc_wald_a$Df[2]`) = `r txt_wald_a_chisq`, *p* = `r txt_wald_a_p`): at least two genres differ in how a change in their playtime relates to a change in wellbeing. Between persons, the test did not reject equality (χ²(`r h2_cc_wald_b$Df[2]`) = `r txt_wald_b_chisq`, *p* = `r txt_wald_b_p`). Under the preregistered criteria, H2a is supported and H2b is not.

```{r}
#| label: h2-joint-test
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# Bayesian analogue of the pre-registered joint Wald test: "are all genre
# within-person coefficients equal?"
# For each MCMC draw, compute the SD of genre within-person effects.  If this
# heterogeneity SD is clearly > 0, at least one genre pair differs.

# Heterogeneity threshold (Methods, SESOI): a spread below sesoi / 1.96 puts
# the 95% prediction interval for a single genre's effect inside the ROPE.
sesoi   <- 0.06
het_thr <- sesoi / qnorm(0.975)
# Share of genres whose effect deviates from the common centre by more than
# the SESOI under a normal spread s (evaluated at each posterior draw).
het_share <- function(s) 2 * (1 - pnorm(sesoi, 0, s))

h2_draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(h2_model)

# brms names fixed effects as b_{varname}
within_cols <- paste0("b_", gh_within)
within_mat  <- as.matrix(h2_draws[, within_cols, drop = FALSE])

genre_effect_sd   <- apply(within_mat, 1, sd)
genre_sd_mean     <- mean(genre_effect_sd)
genre_sd_ci       <- quantile(genre_effect_sd, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
genre_sd_p_thr    <- mean(genre_effect_sd < het_thr)

# Same for between-person effects
between_cols      <- paste0("b_", gh_between)
between_mat       <- as.matrix(h2_draws[, between_cols, drop = FALSE])
genre_between_sd  <- apply(between_mat, 1, sd)
genre_bsd_mean    <- mean(genre_between_sd)
genre_bsd_ci      <- quantile(genre_between_sd, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
genre_bsd_p_thr   <- mean(genre_between_sd < het_thr)
```

```{r}
#| label: txt-genre-differences-h2-2
#| include: false

# Inline quantities for the paragraph(s) below, defined once here so the
# prose reads `r name` rather than a formatting call.
txt_genre_sd_mean <- round(genre_sd_mean, 3)
txt_genre_sd_ci_lo <- round(genre_sd_ci[1], 3)
txt_genre_sd_ci_hi <- round(genre_sd_ci[2], 3)
txt_genre_sd_p_thr_pct <- round(genre_sd_p_thr * 100, 1)
txt_genre_bsd_mean <- round(genre_bsd_mean, 3)
txt_genre_bsd_ci_lo <- round(genre_bsd_ci[1], 3)
txt_genre_bsd_ci_hi <- round(genre_bsd_ci[2], 3)
```

The joint Wald test shows whether the coefficients differ, but not which ones differ or by how much. To estimate the size of the differences from the same model, we computed the SD of the 14 genre coefficients at each posterior draw of the Bayesian fit of M2 and compared it with the heterogeneity threshold of 0.031, the spread at which 95% of genre effects lie inside the ROPE. This statistic and its threshold were not preregistered. Within persons, the SD averaged `r txt_genre_sd_mean` (95% CrI: \[`r txt_genre_sd_ci_lo`, `r txt_genre_sd_ci_hi`\]); the interval lies below the SESOI of 0.06 but crosses the threshold, with `r txt_genre_sd_p_thr_pct`% of the posterior below it (@fig-h2-heterogeneity, blue, top row). Between persons, the SD averaged `r txt_genre_bsd_mean` (95% CrI: \[`r txt_genre_bsd_ci_lo`, `r txt_genre_bsd_ci_hi`\]), above both thresholds. Because the 14 coefficients are estimated independently, their SD includes each coefficient's estimation error, which is large for rarely played genres. The statistic therefore overstates genre heterogeneity and is an upper limit.

```{r}
#| label: integrated-coefs-extract
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# --- M2 (independent coefficients): extract within and between ---
m2_within <- broom.mixed::tidy(h2_model, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(grepl("^gh_.*_within$", term), effect == "fixed") |>
  mutate(
    genre = prettify_genre(sub("^gh_(.*)_within$", "\\1", term)),
    model = "M2: Independent coefficients"
  ) |>
  select(model, genre, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)

m2_between <- broom.mixed::tidy(h2_model, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(grepl("^gh_.*_between$", term), effect == "fixed") |>
  mutate(
    genre = prettify_genre(sub("^gh_(.*)_between$", "\\1", term)),
    model = "M2: Independent coefficients"
  ) |>
  select(model, genre, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)

# --- M4 (multi-membership): extract random slopes + add overall fixed effect ---
# M4's random slopes are deviations from the overall total_within fixed effect.
# To make them comparable to M2/M3's absolute genre coefficients, we add the
# overall total_within fixed effect back to each genre adjustment.
mm_total_within_fe <- fixef(h2_mm_model)["total_within", "Estimate"]

# M4 (multi-membership) group-level effects: genre slope adjustments.
m4_re <- ranef(h2_mm_model)
mm_key <- names(m4_re)[grepl("^mm", names(m4_re))][1]

m4_mm_within <- as.data.frame(m4_re[[mm_key]][, , "total_within"]) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("genre_slug") |>
  mutate(
    genre = prettify_genre(genre_slug),
    model = "M4: Multi-membership",
    # Add overall fixed effect to convert adjustment → absolute
    estimate  = Estimate + mm_total_within_fe,
    std.error = Est.Error,
    conf.low  = Q2.5 + mm_total_within_fe,
    conf.high = Q97.5 + mm_total_within_fe
  ) |>
  select(model, genre, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)

# M4 (multi-membership) between-person: extract random slopes + add overall total_between FE
mm_total_between_fe <- fixef(h2_mm_model)["total_between", "Estimate"]

m4_mm_between <- as.data.frame(m4_re[[mm_key]][, , "total_between"]) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("genre_slug") |>
  mutate(
    genre = prettify_genre(genre_slug),
    model = "M4: Multi-membership",
    estimate  = Estimate + mm_total_between_fe,
    std.error = Est.Error,
    conf.low  = Q2.5 + mm_total_between_fe,
    conf.high = Q97.5 + mm_total_between_fe
  ) |>
  select(model, genre, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)

# --- M3 (hierarchical prior): extract within and between ---
m3_hier_within <- summary(h2_hier_model)$fixed |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
  filter(grepl("^gh_.*_within$", term)) |>
  mutate(
    genre = prettify_genre(sub("^gh_(.*)_within$", "\\1", term)),
    model = "M3: Hierarchical prior",
    estimate  = Estimate,
    std.error = Est.Error,
    conf.low  = `l-95% CI`,
    conf.high = `u-95% CI`
  ) |>
  select(model, genre, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)

m3_hier_between <- summary(h2_hier_model)$fixed |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
  filter(grepl("^gh_.*_between$", term)) |>
  mutate(
    genre = prettify_genre(sub("^gh_(.*)_between$", "\\1", term)),
    model = "M3: Hierarchical prior",
    estimate  = Estimate,
    std.error = Est.Error,
    conf.low  = `l-95% CI`,
    conf.high = `u-95% CI`
  ) |>
  select(model, genre, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)

# --- Combine ---
# Within-person: all three models (M2 FE, M3 Hier, M4 MM)
all_within  <- bind_rows(m2_within, m3_hier_within, m4_mm_within)
# Between-person: all three models (M4 now has full within + between)
all_between <- bind_rows(m2_between, m3_hier_between, m4_mm_between)

# Guard for the Discussion's per-genre paragraph: all 14 within-person
# point estimates lie within a third of the SESOI (|estimate| < 0.02).
stopifnot(max(abs(m3_hier_within$estimate)) < 0.02)

# Per-model interval verdicts and spreads for the per-genre prose
rope_count <- function(d) sum(d$conf.low > -0.06 & d$conf.high < 0.06)
m2_w_in_rope <- rope_count(m2_within)
m2_b_in_rope <- rope_count(m2_between)
m2_w_widths  <- m2_within$conf.high - m2_within$conf.low
m2_widest_genre <- m2_within$genre[which.max(m2_w_widths)]
m2_width_ratio  <- max(m2_w_widths) / min(m2_w_widths)
m4_w_in_rope <- rope_count(m4_mm_within)
m4_b_in_rope <- rope_count(m4_mm_between)
m4_w_range <- range(m4_mm_within$estimate)
m4_b_range <- range(m4_mm_between$estimate)
# Guard the fixed prose: no M2 interval sits entirely outside the ROPE
# ("the remainder straddle a boundary rather than exclude it")
stopifnot(
  all(m2_within$conf.high > -0.06 & m2_within$conf.low < 0.06),
  all(m2_between$conf.high > -0.06 & m2_between$conf.low < 0.06)
)

# Order genres by the M3 (hierarchical prior) within-person estimate; the
# shared y-axis requires a single ordering across both facets.
genre_order_within <- m3_hier_within |> arrange(estimate) |> pull(genre)

all_coefs <- bind_rows(
  all_within  |> mutate(dimension = "Within-person (H2a)"),
  all_between |> mutate(dimension = "Between-person (H2b)")
) |>
  mutate(dimension = factor(dimension, levels = c(
    "Within-person (H2a)", "Between-person (H2b)"
  )))
```

```{r}
#| label: txt-genre-differences-h2-3
#| include: false

# Inline quantities for the paragraph(s) below, defined once here so the
# prose reads `r name` rather than a formatting call.
txt_m2_width_ratio <- round(m2_width_ratio)
txt_m4_w_range_lo <- round(m4_w_range[1], 3)
txt_m4_w_range_hi <- round(m4_w_range[2], 3)
txt_m4_b_range_lo <- round(m4_b_range[1], 3)
txt_m4_b_range_hi <- round(m4_b_range[2], 3)
```

@fig-integrated-coefs (blue circles) shows the per-genre estimates from M2. The 14 within-person point estimates cluster near zero, and `r m2_w_in_rope` of the 14 credible intervals fall entirely inside the ROPE; the remainder straddle a boundary rather than exclude it. The cost of independent estimation shows in the interval widths: the widest within-person interval (`r m2_widest_genre`) is about `r txt_m2_width_ratio` times wider than the narrowest, too wide to support a conclusion about any rarely played genre. Between persons the intervals are wider still, with `r m2_b_in_rope` of the 14 entirely inside the ROPE.

### Exploratory Models (M3 and M4)

```{r}
#| label: h2-hier-tau
#| include: false
#| eval: true

h2_hier_draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(h2_hier_model)

# H2a: within-person genre heterogeneity
tau_draws <- h2_hier_draws$tau_genre_within
tau_mean  <- mean(tau_draws)
tau_ci    <- quantile(tau_draws, c(0.025, 0.975))
tau_in_rope <- mean(tau_draws > -0.06 & tau_draws < 0.06)
tau_p_thr      <- mean(tau_draws < het_thr)
tau_share      <- het_share(tau_draws)
tau_share_mean <- mean(tau_share)
tau_share_ci   <- quantile(tau_share, c(0.025, 0.975))

# H2b: between-person genre heterogeneity
tau_between_draws <- h2_hier_draws$tau_genre_between
tau_between_mean  <- mean(tau_between_draws)
tau_between_ci    <- quantile(tau_between_draws, c(0.025, 0.975))
tau_between_in_rope <- mean(tau_between_draws > -0.06 & tau_between_draws < 0.06)
tau_b_p_thr      <- mean(tau_between_draws < het_thr)
tau_b_share      <- het_share(tau_between_draws)
tau_b_share_mean <- mean(tau_b_share)
tau_b_share_ci   <- quantile(tau_b_share, c(0.025, 0.975))
# Verdict guards for the fixed prose: within negligible, between inconclusive
stopifnot(tau_p_thr > 0.95, tau_b_p_thr < 0.95)
```

```{r}
#| label: h2-mm-sigma
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# sigma_s_within: SD of genre random slopes on total_within
sigma_sw_col <- names(h2_mm_draws)[grepl(
  paste0("sd_", mm_group_name, ".*total_within"),
  names(h2_mm_draws)
)]
if (length(sigma_sw_col) == 0) {
  sigma_sw_col <- names(h2_mm_draws)[grepl("sd_mm.*total_within", names(h2_mm_draws))]
}
stopifnot(length(sigma_sw_col) >= 1)
sigma_sw_col <- sigma_sw_col[1]

sigma_sw_draws       <- h2_mm_draws[[sigma_sw_col]]
sigma_sw_mean        <- mean(sigma_sw_draws)
sigma_sw_ci          <- quantile(sigma_sw_draws, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
sigma_sw_above_sesoi <- mean(sigma_sw_draws > 0.06)
sigma_sw_p_thr       <- mean(sigma_sw_draws < het_thr)
sigma_sw_share       <- het_share(sigma_sw_draws)
sigma_sw_share_mean  <- mean(sigma_sw_share)
sigma_sw_share_ci    <- quantile(sigma_sw_share, c(0.025, 0.975))

# sigma_s_between: SD of genre random slopes on total_between (the full mm()
# formula includes both total_within and total_between in the mm() term)
sigma_sb_col <- names(h2_mm_draws)[grepl(
  paste0("sd_", mm_group_name, ".*total_between"),
  names(h2_mm_draws)
)]
if (length(sigma_sb_col) == 0) {
  sigma_sb_col <- names(h2_mm_draws)[grepl("sd_mm.*total_between", names(h2_mm_draws))]
}
stopifnot(length(sigma_sb_col) >= 1)
sigma_sb_col         <- sigma_sb_col[1]

sigma_sb_draws       <- h2_mm_draws[[sigma_sb_col]]
sigma_sb_mean        <- mean(sigma_sb_draws)
sigma_sb_ci          <- quantile(sigma_sb_draws, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
sigma_sb_above_sesoi <- mean(sigma_sb_draws > 0.06)
sigma_sb_p_thr       <- mean(sigma_sb_draws < het_thr)
sigma_sb_share       <- het_share(sigma_sb_draws)
sigma_sb_share_mean  <- mean(sigma_sb_share)
sigma_sb_share_ci    <- quantile(sigma_sb_share, c(0.025, 0.975))
# Verdict guards for the fixed prose: both M4 dimensions inconclusive
stopifnot(sigma_sw_p_thr < 0.95, sigma_sb_p_thr < 0.95)
```

```{r}
#| label: h2-heterogeneity-extract
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# Reuse draws already extracted in this section:
#   M2: genre_effect_sd / genre_between_sd   (h2-joint-test)
#   M3: tau_draws / tau_between_draws        (h2-hier-tau)
#   M4: sigma_sw_draws / sigma_sb_draws      (h2-mm-sigma)
m2_sd_within_per_draw  <- genre_effect_sd
m2_sd_between_per_draw <- genre_between_sd

h2_het_draws <- bind_rows(
  # Within-person (H2a)
  tibble(dimension = "Within-person (H2a)", model = "M2: Independent coefficients (SD)", value = m2_sd_within_per_draw),
  tibble(dimension = "Within-person (H2a)", model = "M3: Hierarchical prior (τ)", value = tau_draws),
  tibble(dimension = "Within-person (H2a)", model = "M4: Multi-membership (σ_s)", value = sigma_sw_draws),
  # Between-person (H2b)
  tibble(dimension = "Between-person (H2b)", model = "M2: Independent coefficients (SD)", value = m2_sd_between_per_draw),
  tibble(dimension = "Between-person (H2b)", model = "M3: Hierarchical prior (τ)", value = tau_between_draws),
  tibble(dimension = "Between-person (H2b)", model = "M4: Multi-membership (σ_s)", value = sigma_sb_draws)
) |>
  mutate(
    # Reversed so the lowest model (M2) displays at the top
    model = factor(model, levels = c(
      "M4: Multi-membership (σ_s)",
      "M3: Hierarchical prior (τ)",
      "M2: Independent coefficients (SD)"
    )),
    dimension = factor(dimension, levels = c(
      "Within-person (H2a)", "Between-person (H2b)"
    ))
  )
```

```{r}
# Inline quantities for the paragraph(s) below, defined once here so the
# prose reads `r name` rather than a formatting call.
txt_tau_mean <- round(tau_mean, 3)
txt_tau_ci_lo <- round(tau_ci[1], 3)
txt_tau_ci_hi <- round(tau_ci[2], 3)
txt_tau_p_thr_pct <- round(tau_p_thr * 100, 1)
txt_tau_share_mean_pct <- round(tau_share_mean * 100, 1)
txt_tau_share_ci_lo_pct <- round(tau_share_ci[1] * 100, 1)
txt_tau_share_ci_hi_pct <- round(tau_share_ci[2] * 100, 1)
txt_tau_share_n_genres <- round(14 * tau_share_mean, 2)
txt_tau_between_mean <- round(tau_between_mean, 3)
txt_tau_between_ci_lo <- round(tau_between_ci[1], 3)
txt_tau_between_ci_hi <- round(tau_between_ci[2], 3)
txt_tau_b_p_thr_pct <- round(tau_b_p_thr * 100, 1)
txt_tau_b_share_mean_pct <- round(tau_b_share_mean * 100, 1)
txt_tau_b_share_ci_lo_pct <- round(tau_b_share_ci[1] * 100, 1)
txt_tau_b_share_ci_hi_pct <- round(tau_b_share_ci[2] * 100, 1)
txt_tau_b_share_n_genres <- round(14 * tau_b_share_mean, 1)
```

```{r}
#| label: h2-hier-genre-coefs
#| include: false
#| eval: true

hier_within_coefs <- summary(h2_hier_model)$fixed |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(grepl("^gh_.*_within$", term)) |>
  mutate(genre = prettify_genre(sub("^gh_(.*)_within$", "\\1", term)))

hier_between_coefs <- summary(h2_hier_model)$fixed |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(grepl("^gh_.*_between$", term)) |>
  mutate(genre = prettify_genre(sub("^gh_(.*)_between$", "\\1", term)))

n_hier_within_in_rope <- sum(
  hier_within_coefs[["l-95% CI"]] > -0.06 & hier_within_coefs[["u-95% CI"]] < 0.06
)
```

M3 and M4 were specified after the M2 results were known. Under M3, the hierarchical prior model, genre variation in the within-person associations (H2a) is practically negligible: τ~within~ = `r txt_tau_mean` (95% CrI: \[`r txt_tau_ci_lo`, `r txt_tau_ci_hi`\]), with `r txt_tau_p_thr_pct`% of the posterior below the heterogeneity threshold of 0.031 (@fig-h2-heterogeneity, orange). This spread implies that `r txt_tau_share_mean_pct`% of genres (95% CrI \[`r txt_tau_share_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_tau_share_ci_hi_pct`%\]) deviate from the common centre by more than the SESOI, an expected `r txt_tau_share_n_genres` of the 14. Between persons (H2b) the result is inconclusive: τ~between~ = `r txt_tau_between_mean` (95% CrI: \[`r txt_tau_between_ci_lo`, `r txt_tau_between_ci_hi`\]), with `r txt_tau_b_p_thr_pct`% of the posterior below the threshold and an implied `r txt_tau_b_share_mean_pct`% of genres (95% CrI \[`r txt_tau_b_share_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_tau_b_share_ci_hi_pct`%\]) beyond the SESOI, an expected `r txt_tau_b_share_n_genres` of the 14.

Under M4, the multi-membership model, the within-person estimate (H2a) is inconclusive: $\sigma_{s,\text{within}}$ = `r txt_sigma_sw_mean` (95% CrI: \[`r txt_sigma_sw_ci_lo`, `r txt_sigma_sw_ci_hi`\]), with `r txt_sigma_sw_p_thr_pct`% of the posterior below the heterogeneity threshold (@fig-h2-heterogeneity, purple). This spread implies that `r txt_sigma_sw_share_mean_pct`% of genres (95% CrI \[`r txt_sigma_sw_share_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_sigma_sw_share_ci_hi_pct`%\]) deviate from the overall playtime slope by more than the SESOI, an expected `r txt_sigma_sw_share_n_genres` of the 14, and heterogeneity of up to about 0.1 points per hour/day cannot be excluded. The between-person estimate (H2b) is also inconclusive: $\sigma_{s,\text{between}}$ = `r txt_sigma_sb_mean` (95% CrI: \[`r txt_sigma_sb_ci_lo`, `r txt_sigma_sb_ci_hi`\]), with `r txt_sigma_sb_p_thr_pct`% of the posterior below the threshold and an implied `r txt_sigma_sb_share_mean_pct`% of genres (95% CrI \[`r txt_sigma_sb_share_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_sigma_sb_share_ci_hi_pct`%\]) beyond the SESOI. The posterior is concentrated near zero but does not meet the 95% criterion.

::: {.place arguments="auto, scope: \"parent\", float: true"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-h2-heterogeneity
#| fig-cap: "*Genre Heterogeneity Under Three Model Specifications (H2).* Left: within-person (H2a); right: between-person (H2b). M2 (blue) is the preregistered model (SD of its 14 independently estimated coefficients, which includes estimation error); M3 (orange) and M4 (purple) are exploratory (τ and σ~s~, model-estimated spreads). Green band: heterogeneity threshold (0 to 0.031, the spread at which 95% of genre effects lie inside the ROPE of ±0.06). A posterior falling entirely inside the band indicates practically negligible genre heterogeneity. Thick: 66% CrI; thin: 95% CrI."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

ggplot(h2_het_draws, aes(x = value, y = model)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = het_thr,
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "forestgreen", alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = het_thr, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "forestgreen", alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_halfeye(aes(fill = model_family(model)), .width = c(0.66, 0.95),
               alpha = 0.7, point_interval = "median_qi") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = model_palette, guide = "none") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ dimension) +
  labs(x = "Genre heterogeneity (SWEMWBS item-mean per hour/day)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```
:::

The three estimates in @fig-h2-heterogeneity measure the spread of the genre effects in different ways. M2's SD includes estimation error and is an upper limit. M3's τ excludes it and places within-person heterogeneity below the threshold. M4's σ~s~ also excludes it but is less precise, because it describes how the playtime slope changes with the genre composition of a wave rather than how separate genre exposures differ, and its posterior is too wide to decide.

M3 shrinks the per-genre estimates towards their common centre (@fig-integrated-coefs, orange squares): `r n_hier_within_in_rope` of the 14 within-person credible intervals fall entirely inside the ROPE, and the wider between-person intervals show the same pattern.

M4 estimates each genre as a deviation from the overall playtime slope (@fig-integrated-coefs, purple diamonds). With the overall fixed effect added back, its within-person estimates span `r txt_m4_w_range_lo` to `r txt_m4_w_range_hi` and its between-person estimates `r txt_m4_b_range_lo` to `r txt_m4_b_range_hi`.

::: {.place arguments="auto, scope: \"parent\", float: true"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-integrated-coefs
#| fig-cap: "*Per-Genre Exposure Coefficients Under Three Model Specifications (H2).* Left: within-person (H2a); right: between-person (H2b). Each genre row shows M2 (blue circle; preregistered model, no pooling), M3 (orange square; exploratory, hierarchical prior), and M4 (purple diamond; exploratory, multi-membership). The M2 series is the caterpillar plot specified in the preregistration. Genres ordered by the M3 within-person estimate. Green band: ROPE (±0.06). Thick bars: ±1 posterior SD; thin bars: 95% CrI."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

# Factor order: M2 top within each genre row, M4 bottom.
# position_dodge with a vertical y-axis places the LAST level at the top,
# so we reverse the desired visual order in the factor levels.
model_levels <- c("M4: Multi-membership", "M3: Hierarchical prior", "M2: Independent coefficients")
model_status_labels <- c(
  "M2: Independent coefficients" = "M2: Independent coefficients (preregistered)",
  "M3: Hierarchical prior" = "M3: Hierarchical prior (exploratory)",
  "M4: Multi-membership" = "M4: Multi-membership (exploratory)"
)

ggplot(all_coefs |>
         mutate(genre = factor(genre, levels = genre_order_within),
                model = factor(model, levels = model_levels)),
       aes(x = estimate, y = genre, shape = model, colour = model)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -0.06, xmax = 0.06,
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "forestgreen", alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-0.06, 0.06), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "forestgreen", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
                 linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = estimate - std.error, xmax = estimate + std.error),
                 linewidth = 1,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("M2: Independent coefficients" = 16,
                                 "M3: Hierarchical prior" = 15,
                                 "M4: Multi-membership" = 18),
                     breaks = c("M2: Independent coefficients", "M3: Hierarchical prior", "M4: Multi-membership"),
                     labels = model_status_labels) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("M2: Independent coefficients" = unname(model_palette["M2"]),
                                  "M3: Hierarchical prior" = unname(model_palette["M3"]),
                                  "M4: Multi-membership" = unname(model_palette["M4"])),
                      breaks = c("M2: Independent coefficients", "M3: Hierarchical prior", "M4: Multi-membership"),
                      labels = model_status_labels) +
  facet_wrap(~ dimension) +
  labs(x = "Genre coefficient (SWEMWBS item-mean per hour/day)",
       y = NULL, shape = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```
:::

In sum, the preregistered test shows that the within-person genre coefficients are not all equal, and no model places the within-person differences at practical significance: they are negligible under M3 and inconclusive but small under M2 and M4. Between persons, M3 and M4 are inconclusive, and M2's SD, an upper limit inflated by the wide between-person intervals, does not constrain the spread. On neither dimension does any model show a genre that differs meaningfully from the rest. Genre terms do not improve out-of-sample prediction (Appendix D), and the wide intervals for rarely played genres rule out confident inference about any single genre. Appendix E (@tbl-hypothesis-summary) tabulates the heterogeneity estimates and convergence diagnostics for the three models; full posterior summaries for all four models are in the supplementary materials.

## Daily Timescale (Exploratory)

```{r}
#| label: daily-fits
#| cache: false   # loads brms fits from models/*.rds; caching would serialise GBs
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# ---- Fits ------------------------------------------------------------------
d_m1_ls   <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m1_daily_ls.rds"))
d_m1_full <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m1_daily_ls_full.rds"))
d_m1_ar   <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m1_daily_ls_ar.rds"))
d_m1_wh   <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m1_daily_ls_wh.rds"))
d_m1_xfl  <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m1_daily_ls_xfl.rds"))
d_xfl_dr  <- posterior::as_draws_df(d_m1_xfl)
d_rx_b1    <- mean(d_xfl_dr$b_xfl_within)
d_rx_b1_ci <- quantile(d_xfl_dr$b_xfl_within, c(.025, .975))
d_m3_ls   <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m3_daily_ls_v2.rds"))
d_m4_ls   <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m4_daily_mm_ls.rds"))

stopifnot(nobs(d_m1_ls) == sum(!is.na(daily_frame$life_sat)))

d_extract_m1 <- function(fit, sesoi) {
  dr <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit)
  w <- dr$b_total_within
  b <- dr$b_total_between
  s <- dr$sd_pid__total_within
  list(
    b1 = mean(w), b1_ci = quantile(w, c(.025, .975)),
    b1_rope = mean(abs(w) < sesoi),
    b2 = mean(b), b2_ci = quantile(b, c(.025, .975)),
    b2_rope = mean(abs(b) < sesoi),
    sd_slope = mean(s), sd_slope_ci = quantile(s, c(.025, .975)),
    sd_slope_above = mean(s > sesoi),
    rhat = max(brms::rhat(fit), na.rm = TRUE),
    divs = sum(subset(brms::nuts_params(fit), Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)
  )
}
d_extract_m3 <- function(fit, sesoi) {
  dr <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit)
  tw <- dr$tau_genre_within
  tb <- dr$tau_genre_between
  list(
    tau_w = mean(tw), tau_w_ci = quantile(tw, c(.025, .975)),
    tau_w_rope = mean(tw < sesoi),
    tau_b = mean(tb), tau_b_ci = quantile(tb, c(.025, .975)),
    tau_b_rope = mean(tb < sesoi),
    rhat = max(brms::rhat(fit), na.rm = TRUE),
    divs = sum(subset(brms::nuts_params(fit), Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)
  )
}
d_r1  <- d_extract_m1(d_m1_ls, d_primary)
d_r1f <- d_extract_m1(d_m1_full, d_primary)
d_r1a <- d_extract_m1(d_m1_ar, d_primary)
d_r1w <- d_extract_m1(d_m1_wh, d_primary)
d_ar1_draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(d_m1_ar)[["ar[1]"]]
d_ar1 <- mean(d_ar1_draws)
d_r3  <- d_extract_m3(d_m3_ls, d_primary)

# Draw vectors kept for the daily figure
d_dr1 <- posterior::as_draws_df(d_m1_ls)
d_dr3 <- posterior::as_draws_df(d_m3_ls)

d_m4_draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(d_m4_ls)
d_sw_col <- names(d_m4_draws)[grepl("sd_mm.*total_within", names(d_m4_draws))]
d_sb_col <- names(d_m4_draws)[grepl("sd_mm.*total_between", names(d_m4_draws))]
stopifnot(length(d_sw_col) == 1, length(d_sb_col) == 1)
d_sigma_sw       <- mean(d_m4_draws[[d_sw_col]])
d_sigma_sw_ci    <- quantile(d_m4_draws[[d_sw_col]], c(.025, .975))
d_sigma_sw_below <- mean(d_m4_draws[[d_sw_col]] < d_primary)
d_sigma_sb       <- mean(d_m4_draws[[d_sb_col]])
d_sigma_sb_ci    <- quantile(d_m4_draws[[d_sb_col]], c(.025, .975))
d_sigma_sb_below <- mean(d_m4_draws[[d_sb_col]] < d_primary)

# M2-D: independent-coefficient genre specification. Its heterogeneity summary
# is the per-draw SD across the 14 genre coefficients, which includes
# estimation error (sampling-noise inflation), as in the registered M2.
d_m2_ls    <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m2_daily_ls.rds"))
d_m2_draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(d_m2_ls)
d_m2_wcols <- grep("^b_gh_.*_w$", names(d_m2_draws), value = TRUE)
d_m2_bcols <- grep("^b_gh_.*_b$", names(d_m2_draws), value = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(d_m2_wcols) == 14, length(d_m2_bcols) == 14)
d_m2_sdw_draws <- apply(as.matrix(d_m2_draws[, d_m2_wcols]), 1, sd)
d_m2_sdb_draws <- apply(as.matrix(d_m2_draws[, d_m2_bcols]), 1, sd)
d_m2_sdw       <- mean(d_m2_sdw_draws)
d_m2_sdw_ci    <- quantile(d_m2_sdw_draws, c(.025, .975))
d_m2_sdw_below <- mean(d_m2_sdw_draws < d_primary)
d_m2_sdb       <- mean(d_m2_sdb_draws)
d_m2_sdb_ci    <- quantile(d_m2_sdb_draws, c(.025, .975))
d_m2_sdb_below <- mean(d_m2_sdb_draws < d_primary)

# Heterogeneity threshold at the daily scale (Methods, SESOI): d_primary / 1.96,
# and the implied share of genres deviating from the centre by > SESOI.
d_het_thr        <- d_primary / qnorm(0.975)
d_het_share      <- function(s) 2 * (1 - pnorm(d_primary, 0, s))
d_tau_w_thr      <- mean(d_dr3$tau_genre_within  < d_het_thr)
d_tau_b_thr      <- mean(d_dr3$tau_genre_between < d_het_thr)
d_sigma_sw_thr   <- mean(d_m4_draws[[d_sw_col]] < d_het_thr)
d_sigma_sb_thr   <- mean(d_m4_draws[[d_sb_col]] < d_het_thr)
d_m2_sdw_thr     <- mean(d_m2_sdw_draws < d_het_thr)
d_m2_sdb_thr     <- mean(d_m2_sdb_draws < d_het_thr)
d_tau_w_share    <- mean(d_het_share(d_dr3$tau_genre_within))
d_sigma_sw_share <- mean(d_het_share(d_m4_draws[[d_sw_col]]))
d_m2_rhat <- max(brms::rhat(d_m2_ls), na.rm = TRUE)
d_m2_divs <- sum(subset(brms::nuts_params(d_m2_ls),
                        Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)

# M4-D H1 estimates via its total-playtime fixed effects (mirrors the
# biweekly M1-vs-M4 consistency check in @fig-h1-all-models)
d_m4_b1      <- mean(d_m4_draws$b_total_within)
d_m4_b1_ci   <- quantile(d_m4_draws$b_total_within, c(.025, .975))
d_m4_b1_rope <- mean(abs(d_m4_draws$b_total_within) < d_primary)
d_m4_b2      <- mean(d_m4_draws$b_total_between)
d_m4_b2_ci   <- quantile(d_m4_draws$b_total_between, c(.025, .975))
d_m4_b2_rope <- mean(abs(d_m4_draws$b_total_between) < d_primary)
d_m4_rhat <- max(brms::rhat(d_m4_ls), na.rm = TRUE)
d_m4_divs <- sum(subset(brms::nuts_params(d_m4_ls), Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)

```

```{r}
txt_d_sigma_sb <- round(d_sigma_sb, 2)
txt_d_sigma_sb_ci_lo <- round(d_sigma_sb_ci[1], 2)
txt_d_sigma_sb_ci_hi <- round(d_sigma_sb_ci[2], 2)
txt_pct_d_sigma_sb_thr <- round(100 * d_sigma_sb_thr, 1)
txt_d_m2_sdb <- round(d_m2_sdb, 2)
txt_d_m2_sdb_ci_lo <- round(d_m2_sdb_ci[1], 2)
txt_d_m2_sdb_ci_hi <- round(d_m2_sdb_ci[2], 2)
```

The daily refits (M1-D to M4-D) were not preregistered, and every estimate in this section is exploratory. Participants in the analysed daily sample contribute a median of `r d_median_days` diary days, with participation declining from `r txt_d_day1_n` responses on day 1 to `r txt_d_day30_n` on day 30; windows close at the survey completion timestamp (median length `r txt_d_wh_med` hours), so `r txt_pct_d_zero_play`% of person-days record no console or PC play.

@fig-daily-posteriors displays the posteriors against the ROPE. At the daily level, the within-person association between same-day playtime and life satisfaction was positive, at β = `r txt_d_r1_b1` points per additional hour in the standalone total-playtime model (M1-D; 95% CrI \[`r txt_d_r1_b1_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_r1_b1_ci_hi`\]), with the lower credible bound at zero and the entire posterior inside the ROPE (`r txt_pct_d_r1_b1_rope`%); the multi-membership model's fixed effect is similar (M4-D: β = `r txt_d_m4_b1`, 95% CrI \[`r txt_d_m4_b1_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_m4_b1_ci_hi`\]). The interval widens past zero under two of the three robustness refits (Appendix D). Person-to-person variation in this slope was practically negligible: the random-slope SD was `r txt_d_r1_sd_slope` (95% CrI \[`r txt_d_r1_sd_slope_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_r1_sd_slope_ci_hi`\]), with `r txt_pct_d_sd_slope_below`% of the posterior below the SESOI. Between persons, with habitual play measured in full-day hours, participants who play more than others reported slightly lower daily life satisfaction: M1-D gives β = `r txt_d_r1_b2` points per habitual daily hour (95% CrI \[`r txt_d_r1_b2_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_r1_b2_ci_hi`\]), a negative lean whose posterior sits `r txt_pct_d_r1_b2_rope`% inside the ROPE; M4-D gives β = `r txt_d_m4_b2` (95% CrI \[`r txt_d_m4_b2_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_m4_b2_ci_hi`\]); and the all-responses refit, which scores unobserved play as zero, gives β = `r txt_d_r1f_b2` (95% CrI \[`r txt_d_r1f_b2_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_r1f_b2_ci_hi`\]) (@tbl-daily-summary).

Genre heterogeneity at the daily level showed the same pattern as at the biweekly level, judged against the daily heterogeneity threshold of `r txt_d_het_thr` slider points (1 ÷ 1.96). Within persons, the hierarchical prior places heterogeneity below the threshold: τ~within~ = `r txt_d_r3_tau_w` (95% CrI \[`r txt_d_r3_tau_w_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_r3_tau_w_ci_hi`\]), with `r txt_pct_d_tau_w_thr`% of its posterior below it and an implied `r txt_pct_d_tau_w_share`% of genres beyond the SESOI. The multi-membership model is inconclusive, σ~s,within~ = `r txt_d_sigma_sw` (95% CrI \[`r txt_d_sigma_sw_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_sigma_sw_ci_hi`\]; `r txt_pct_d_sigma_sw_thr`% below the threshold), as is M2-D, whose SD across the 14 independently estimated genre coefficients of `r txt_d_m2_sdw` (95% CrI \[`r txt_d_m2_sdw_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_m2_sdw_ci_hi`\]) is computed at each posterior draw and noise-inflated, as at the biweekly level (`r txt_pct_d_m2_sdw_thr`% below the threshold). The between-person results are inconclusive: τ~between~ = `r txt_d_r3_tau_b` (95% CrI \[`r txt_d_r3_tau_b_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_r3_tau_b_ci_hi`\]) has `r txt_pct_d_tau_b_thr`% of its posterior below the threshold; σ~s,between~ = `r txt_d_sigma_sb` (95% CrI \[`r txt_d_sigma_sb_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_sigma_sb_ci_hi`\]) has `r txt_pct_d_sigma_sb_thr`%; and M2-D's between-person raw SD (`r txt_d_m2_sdb`, 95% CrI \[`r txt_d_m2_sdb_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_m2_sdb_ci_hi`\]) sits far above it, with the usual estimation-error inflation.

## Robustness

Three sensitivity analyses test whether the conclusions depend on analytic choices. None changes a conclusion. Adjusting for age, gender, and ethnicity shifts the H1 coefficients by less than 0.01 points and changes no ROPE verdict (Appendix D, @tbl-sensitivity-demo). Halving or doubling the heterogeneity hyperprior scales leaves the H2 parameters essentially unchanged (Appendix D, @tbl-prior-sensitivity). Refitting on multiply imputed data (m = 100) reproduces the H1 equivalence under the preregistered 90% CI rule (equivalence tests are two one-sided tests at α = .05, which correspond to a 90% rather than a 95% interval; @lakensEquivalenceTestsPractical2017a) and rejects genre-coefficient equality in neither pooled dimension (Appendix D, @tbl-sensitivity-imputation). Full specifications, results, and diagnostics for all three analyses, together with the predictive model comparison, are reported in Appendix D.

# Discussion

When previous work has reported that time spent gaming carries no meaningful association with wellbeing, a common objection is that surely it must depend on the type of game one plays. After all, a relaxing puzzle game and a competitive shooter should not plausibly have the same effect on the person playing them. Video game heterogeneity is the standing explanation for why aggregate playtime nulls should not be taken at face value: playtime is a poorly specified exposure whose associations average over distinct causal contrasts [@ballouHowVideoGames2025; @magnusson2024harmful], and a null total association can in principle be produced by heterogeneous true effects that offset in aggregate [@yarkoniGeneralizabilityCrisis2022]. Genre is the most widely used name for those contrasts [@starostaTangledWaysClassify2024], which makes it the natural first place to look.
